# Template: staff privacy notice for a centre using ActivityRoster

Adapt the square-bracketed parts. Give it to every instructor and volunteer when they
join, and link it in ActivityRoster under Office → Settings → "Your centre's privacy
notice".

---

**[Centre name] — how we use your information**

We are [centre name], [address]. We are the data controller for the information below.
Contact [name] at [email] with any question.

**What we hold.** Your name, email and phone; your date of birth (so we can apply the
right working-hours rules if you're under 18); your RYA and other qualifications with
their expiry dates; your DBS/PVG/AccessNI/Garda vetting status and dates; your availability,
shifts, hours worked, leave and pay rate; an emergency contact; for under-18s, a parent or
guardian's contact details and their written permission.

**Why.** To roster you safely and lawfully (instructor ratios, safety-boat cover,
qualification checks), to meet our safeguarding duties, to pay you, and to keep the
records employment and RYA recognition require. Our lawful bases are your contract or
volunteer agreement, legal obligations, and our legitimate interest in running the centre.

**Who sees it.** Centre admins see everything above. Other instructors see your name and
shift times only. [If you are under 18, your contact details are visible only to admins
and the welfare officer.] We use ActivityRoster (ActiveRoster Ltd, company number 17505500) to store and process
this information on our behalf; it is hosted in the UK/EU and never sold or used for
anything else. Their notice is at activityroster.com/privacy.

**How long.** While you work with us and for [12 months] after your last shift, so you
can return next season. Hours and pay records are kept for [6 years] as the law
requires. Vetting documents are deleted when your profile is.

**Your rights.** You can ask for a copy of your information, correct it, ask us to delete
it, or object. Ask [name] or use activityroster.com/privacy-request. You can complain to
the ICO (ico.org.uk) [or the Data Protection Commission, dataprotection.ie].
